requirements.requirement: The system must include a malpractice object in the provider detail API response payload.
The system must populate the malpractice object using the output from EVAL-P-MALPRACTICE-LOGIC-001 without transformation loss.
The system must include evidence_links in the malpractice object as an array of valid URLs.
The system must expose a field that explicitly distinguishes between unknown data and confirmed absence of malpractice actions.
The system must preserve null values for unknown malpractice fields rather than coercing them to false or zero.
The system must ensure the malpractice object is included in all evaluate_care_facade provider evaluation responses.
The system must maintain backward compatibility such that existing API consumers do not break when the malpractice object is added.
The system must ensure the malpractice object conforms to the schema defined in EVAL-P-MALPRACTICE-SCHEMA-001.
The system must return an empty malpractice object with unknown flags when no data is available instead of omitting the field.
The system must integrate the malpractice object into the tool_router response format without breaking routing or parsing.
The system must ensure LLM-consumable responses include the malpractice object in a deterministic and stable field location.
The system must ensure LLM responses do not infer positive quality from absence of malpractice data.
The system must ensure LLM responses correctly interpret unknown malpractice data as uncertainty rather than cleanliness.
The system must ensure LLM responses reference evidence_links when explaining malpractice signals.
The system must ensure LLM responses degrade provider evaluation when malpractice signals are present.
The system must ensure LLM responses do not hallucinate malpractice data when the malpractice object is empty or unknown.
The system must return a valid API response even if malpractice logic fails, with malpractice marked as unknown.
The system must log an error when malpractice data retrieval or transformation fails without blocking the full provider response.
